terms.gloss: rely on, rest on, lean on
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent: with the ablative, or in and the ablative
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.122: quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur
Traupman 96, 297: potes nītī mē, you can count on me
terms.comment: Properly “lean on, press against”, then “rely on” whatever holds one up: spē nītī (Cic. Att. 3.9.2, Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short give the perfect as nīsus or nixus. To depend on someone for one’s keep is to be fed by them: Ā parentibus adhūc alitur, he still depends on his parents (M-O s.v. support: dependent).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, semi-deponent: with the dative of a person, the ablative of a thing
evidence: Cic. Att. 8.13.2: illum, quō anteā cōnfīdēbant, metuunt (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Cas. 348: omnēs mortālēs dīs sunt frētī

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, semi-deponent, with the dative or ablative

phrases.latin: Est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī exque iīs dēligere optimōs et probātissimōs, quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur
phrases.english: It is a young man’s part, then, to respect his elders and to choose from among them the best and most approved, on whose advice and authority he can rely
where will you run to? what will you rely on?

phrases.latin: nam omnēs mortālēs dīs sunt frētī, sed tamen vīdī ego dīs frētōs saepe multōs dēcipī
phrases.english: for all men rely on the gods; and yet I have often seen many who relied on the gods let down
